paper_finding: 18 of 30 agents chose the identical git branch name and over half built the same kind of project unprompted
note: four agent runs over one Program came back with two distinct subjects, two Property classes and three distinct claims; the harness emits the numbers rather than assuming either way, and a Program whose agents came back with nothing reads as zeroes

paper_finding: when one agent makes a bad decision it is likely that many agents will make that same bad decision
note: tasks_live_dedup_idx already refused two live Tasks naming one Hypothesis; the shape it does not refuse is two Hypotheses about one subject and one Property class, which is what the scheduler arm now declines while the first run holds it and admits the moment that run ends

paper_finding: agents given a job queue escalated to polling 30 times a second, one run making 2.4 million requests for 117 accepted jobs
mechanism: rk2_egress_reserve, against the Program's compiled budget_requests
note: twenty-five requests past an exhausted budget are answered 407 with a typed reason at the door; no name was resolved, no socket opened and the target saw nothing, and the engagement's record stays at what it actually spent while the loop is counted separately

paper_finding: on hidden-profile tasks models scored 17-36% against a solo ceiling near 100%
mechanism: roles.max_concurrent for validator, and open_validation_session's refusal
note: the roster runs one validator session at a time and a second is refused by name, so there is no group here whose belief could displace a private fact; the mode is not reachable rather than absent

paper_finding: consensus is not evidence, and the packet is where that is either true or not
note: a peer's claim about the same subject judged to a verdict and a third agent opening a candidate beside the open session change the document by nothing; the packet reaches no column of verdicts, validation_attempts, validation_queue or review_gates, and its key list is pinned so a field carrying a peer's conclusion fails the suite

paper_finding: agents disabled each other's Unix accounts and killed competing processes
note: every child runs read-only as uid 65534 with cap-drop ALL, no-new-privileges, a tmpfs scratch of its own and no engine socket, so there is no account to disable and no process of another child to signal; the canonical rows are written through verbs the database authorises per Program

paper_finding: agents planted code disguised as another agent's
mechanism: isolation.own_home, the per-run copy the configured home is a template for
note: one host directory per installation was mounted writable at HOME into every child, so what one child wrote the next child read and could not tell from its own; the configured directory is now a template nothing mounts, each run is handed a copy of it with the modes it had, and the copy is removed when the run ends -- a second child finds what the operator seeded and nothing the first child left

paper_finding: given contradictory directives on a shared machine, agents reached each other
mechanism: isolation.held, an exclusive per-network claim the launch holds across the check
note: one_peer was a check-then-act over one network name per installation, and a peer attached inside the launch window was reachable from the child; the launch now takes an exclusive lock on the network name and holds it across the check and the child, so a second launch made from inside the first's window is refused by name across processes as well as threads, and what one_peer still answers is a peer attached by something that is not a launch
